The setup for Torben Betts’s new political thriller is an unlikely one: a successful New York journalist in the 1960s hires a new nanny, then proceeds to draw her into a dangerous investigative reporting project, before ultimately ending up in an effective hostage situation.
Bett s ‘s writing and Trevor Nunn’s production both fail to grip and are hampered by a stilted talkiness .

Betts aims to write an accessible plot that can start a conversation, rather than test your knowledge. Also, the title ‘Speculations’ is bound to raise eyebrows, especially when five out of six cast members are based on real people. Ultimately, the play acts to speculate on Kilgallen’s original theories.
Speculations doesn't quite live up to its promise and stops short of connecting the dots between these cases.

cn.t: Betts' conspiracy thriller about Dorothy Kilgallen receives a lukewarm response, with critics finding the premise intriguing but execution underwhelming despite Nunn's direction and Dee's performance.
